verdict.tagline: Relaxing home renovations hampered by clunky controls and technical flaws.
for_you_if: you enjoy methodical cleaning and interior design tasks
you can overlook awkward camera angles and clumsy menus
you want a satisfying property restoration loop
not_for_you_if: you need smooth controls and flexible key binding
you cannot tolerate game crashes or lost save data
you are sensitive to startup advertisements

claims.claim: Reviewers report that moving furniture to access and repair electrical sockets prevents the furniture from being placed back in its original position without blocking the repaired outlets.

citations.review_text:
REVIEW #138
House Flipper
----------

This is what I call, "'tism torture."

In House Flipper, a main game mechanic is to repair and update houses per a customer's specification. At one point, I entered a house to paint it and repair some busted electrical sockets. I found the sockets behind furniture and kitchen cabinetry, so I moved both items and repair the sockets. However, since they were fixed, I couldn't rearrange the rooms back to how they were before because the working outlets would be blocked. In the kitchen, this completely threw off how all of the cabinets were lining up. This is something that's completely incompatible with my OCD and high functioning autistic brain.

Also, the starter mop looks really odd, the mopping animation seems to barely exist, and it's sometimes difficult to make out dirt textures. Plus, the door opening sound feels ripped from a 2000s instant messaging program, and it pulls me out of the game experience every time that I hear it. There may be more to hate or love this game, but I got about 3-4 homes deep into this thing, and I can't convince myself to do more.

Lots of people love House Flipper, and for sure, I think it's an awesome concept. I also admit to having some fun when starting out in the game (albeit with a bit of aggravation from the aforementioned aspects.) However, too many details of this title evoke irritation in my soul. Again, people seem to love this thing, so I'm sure that my point of view may not align with many who read this review. Regardless, I'll stand my ground on the opinion that this game (or at least, this original version of HF1) could've used more polish.

No, House Flipper. You are not allowed to stay on my PC. I don't care how drunk you are. Go home.

Incredibly buggy game. You need to move everything to find where the broken electrical outlet is but can't put the items back in their original position. This game has been the bane of my existence and I don't think I'll play again

claims.claim: Reviewers report performance issues including lag and poor optimization.

citations.review_text:
Okay, despite me giving this game a positive rating, I do need to preface by saying this game is NOT for everyone!!

Now originally, I intended on buying House Flipper 2, since I heard very good things about it. However, seeing that 39.99 price tag, I said "hell nah" and looked at the og instead. I felt that 24.99  was STILL a bit steep, given the games age, but I was too curious to turn away.

Now, after playing for a short while, I really do enjoy it. I've always loved older games (before you hate me, I know 2018 isn't THAT old, but compared to most sims nowadays? this is pretty much a relic in terms of graphics), and this one has an incredible charm to it. There's tons of tools that you use, each task feels simple yet unique, and the houses are honestly really fun to search through. That does not mean its without faults. The graphics are nothing spectacular, which is what I expected from the get-go. There is lag, especially if you use your actual keyboard to play (I found that using a controller actually helped the framerate and just overall made the experience more smooth). However, I did not find these issues to personally affect my enjoyment (I've emulated trashy PS1 and N64 games, so this is really nothing annoying for me).

Is it worth 25 bucks? That, reader, is for you to determine. If you like casual gameplay where you really don't have to think too hard + you like to decorate however you want + don't mind having mediocre framerate. Then yeah, maybe this is up your alley! 

Me, personally? I'm not too happy on the price tag. This game is pushing a decade old, it should honestly not be more than 15, especially given there is a remaster version out (also, why the hell is the remastered version so expensive??). Will I be refunding? No. I actually really enjoy the repetitive nature of this game, even if I do feel it was pricey for what its worth. 

Damn you Frozen Disrtict, you caught another helpless soul in your grasps!!
It's a game where you fix houses, yet it runs so badly, standing ovation for the optimization

cohorts.summary: Players settling into the routine note limited mission variety alongside clunky customization tools, though the core tasks remain engaging.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that painting tasks can feel annoying to perform.

citations.review_text: A very fun game. Main issues is painting is really annoying, and there's not enough email jobs.

Rating: 9.1/10

House Flipper is a relaxing and surprisingly addictive simulation game that turns the process of buying, renovating, decorating, and selling houses into an enjoyable gameplay loop. Players start with simple renovation jobs such as cleaning, painting, repairing, and furnishing rooms before gradually building up their skills, tools, and finances. What begins as basic maintenance quickly develops into a satisfying progression system where players can take on larger and more ambitious projects.

One of the game's biggest strengths is how rewarding the renovation process feels. Cleaning a completely neglected house, repairing damaged areas, choosing new furniture, and transforming empty rooms into something presentable creates a strong sense of progression. The wide variety of tools and customization options allows players to approach projects in different ways, while the career system provides enough structure to keep the experience moving forward. The gameplay is also easy to pick up, making it particularly enjoyable for players who prefer relaxing simulations without constant pressure.

The game can become somewhat repetitive, especially when performing similar renovation tasks over longer sessions, and some mechanics are more basic than they initially appear. However, the satisfying progression and relaxing gameplay loop make it easy to overlook these limitations. House Flipper is an excellent choice for players who enjoy simulation, renovation, interior design, and creative games where completing small tasks gradually leads to much larger projects.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the user interface and the process of customizing homes as clunky and overly complex.

citations.review_text: This game is incredibly clunky. A key feature of the "work" genre of games is that the UI has to be satisfying and smooth. This game is overly clicky, and has too many obstacles in the way of repeating tasks. The deeper gameplay of customizing homes to buyers' tastes is needlessly obfuscated and clunkified.

citations.review_text: I eat, sleep and breathe this game. It is perfect in terms of having a lot of the process/logistics behind actual housework, while still being quite fun and not too repetitive. While there are some limitations with building houses it is a very enjoyable game and well made. There are a few bugs that I would research before buying but it is overall a very fun game and I do not regret the money I spent on this. I was lucky to get the game for free while it was on sale and then as I started to play it more I decided to buy the extension packs. Some limitations I had issues with were: 1. Unable to make a basement/elevated house if you're building it from scratch. 2. Minimal item options in a few categories (balcony types, outdoor-flooring types, etc) 3. All items must snap to a very specific grid and cannot be free moved. This being said however I still enjoy the game a lot and look forward to spending every waking hour playing this.

Man I love house flipper, I wish there were options to build your own house fully. Game play is fun and its a great cozy game. Would love to see if there were improvements in game play and options in  house flipper 2 and the remastered collection. If you get this on sale def recc!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that subscribing to workshop items can cause the game to crash, lag, and experience extremely long loading times.

citations.review_text:
To be honest I have mixed feelings about the game. The game concept I truly love. I have bought almost all the DLCs. I really enjoy designing the houses to either sell or rent. I like what the DLCs add to the game. 

The issues I have is how the game runs. At one point, i subscribed to some workshop items. But the game started crashing and running badly. So I had to unsubscribe to ALL of them. There are only a handful I wanted. I just wanted a Jeep, Herbie the Lovebug, and a few items to make a recording studio in my "office". So I got rid of them, but the game still takes FOREVER to load. When I click continue game or go to any job or back to my office, it sometimes takes up to five minutes to even load. It also screen tears and lags. It does not matter how many items are in a house. I have watched my RAM to see if it spikes. The only time that seemed to be an issue was with the workshop items, ever since I got rid of those it never spikes up here, even when it glitches or lags. 

It honestly disappointing how bad the game is running. This is the only game I have these issues with. So, based on how fun the game is, I will recommend it, but I would also be weary about how the game may run. I'm still continuing to play, because I really enjoy it, I just wish it was running better.

Honestly, this game is pretty satisfying and even kind of fun, in fact it's a blast and I have to recommend it whole heartedly. The negative reviews on this game are funny so let's have fun with that.

To start with this game is for creatives. You know the people who shop at Goodwill and can enhance, change and create something incredibly unique with the help of a design gun (found in your arsenal of tools) to make your furniture cozy. 

Second, the lighting in this game is adjustable. The lighting can be adjusted two different ways - one in your computer settings/game settings OR in the game itself by clicking on each lamp or light fixture. Reading the devs explanation on the community tab helps. I mean if you're not too busy complaining about the lighting to look. 

Third, some of the DLC maps have small rooms which test your design skills. This isn't the Sims where everything is already fit exactly perfectly. You have to use imagination and think like an engineer. But hey it's a video game after all. 

Fourth, there's bugs that are being addressed and updated on a regular basis. Join the Discord server and voice your concerns there instead of in a review of the game. Helps the devs address them and won't give the Steam audience a bad impression of the game. 

Lastly, and most importantly, this game can be played independently without all the DLCS but they add on many new and exciting features - building an entire house from scratch, acquiring cool new tools like the duplicate gun (for example) and giving you an opportunity to experience the game as it was intended. If price point is your concern maybe this isn't for you. I bought all the DLC's especially remastered and I love it! 

Overall, while i love the concept I question the negative reviews about this game. It delivers what it offers and it's longevity speaks more volumes than someone who wants the Taj Mahal for the price of a Happy Meal. It's more than satisfying and it's a really fun game to play.

Frozen Way? More like EA.

To start, I want to say that I enjoy this game. As a creative person I love decorating and designing. I like being able to go in and clean up a house, and I like all the little minigames where you put things together and the painting/tiling. But this game REALLY lacks in the decorating and designing part of house flipping. Almost all of the furniture is either very basic or minimalist and modern so you're very limited in what kind of decor style you want to do unless you buy the overpriced DLC. The creators of this game really enjoy pumping out DLCs. The only saving grace is the workshop which can kind of allow you to add some more variety to your furniture and decorating.

The game is still pretty buggy and the lighting is terrible, but from what I've seen the lighting hasn't been improved in HF2 or the remastered edition. I genuinely can't recommend getting this game unless it's on sale.

citations.review_text: House flipper OG is a great game. What angers me is the clear greed from Frozen. You guys really took the same game and added more content that couldve been added to the original game in an update, and youre selling it for over $30? (remastered edition) cmon guys, thats plain greed. Just update the original game or give the "remastered" to those who bought it already for free rather than charging over $30 for the EXACT SAME GAME just with ONE update and different lighting.( $25 if you buy the bundle of DLCs however i have all of those and paid way too much to just go "heres $20 for the exact same thing i already paid for!" )  take notes from the creators of "Wolf quest" who did what should be done, they remastered in an even bigger way than frozen district has and gave the original players the new game for free seeing as they already paid for it just an older verison without the new "content" that equals an update not even dlc, and new players paid full price for the game, as it should be. youre basically just adding updates and calling it an entirley new game then charging your customers as if it was an entirley new game. sililarily to house flipper 2. Shame on you frozen district.

This game has many QoL features that were never implemented and is missing a lot of polish. In the meantime, they then release a sequel. Then, instead of finishing that sequel and adding needed content, they chose to make a "remaster" of this game (which is only 8 years old and still completely fine). They could have just improved on this game, but they saw an opportunity to grift people into buying a new copy of a game they might already own, and then all new DLC to go along with it - and that's not even counting the sequel. Don't support greedy developers.
